messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: hf-artifact-fetch-errors (sev2) — multiple model fetch failures detected for hosted model catalog. Paging oncall: @Maya (oncall). Logs show 429s from huggingface.co during manifest/artifact GETs.

Maya (oncall): I'm on it. Initial triage — are we seeing user-facing errors or just cold-start delays?

Luca (support): Customers reported slow responses and some 5xx on first requests for a few apps. Support ticket #1209 mentions model pull timed out.

Jamal (eng-sre): Confirming 429 spikes from HF in our fetch logs. Sample: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:02Z GET https://huggingface.co/models/redwood/opt-13b/resolve/main/config.json 429 rate limit exceeded
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z GET https://huggingface.co/models/redwood/opt-13b/resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin 429 rate limit exceeded
```
We have retries but backoff is triggering cascade due to many cold starts.

Sofia (runtime): Impact profile — cold-starts that need model fetch from HF are timing out, so endpoints fall back to error 503. Warm instances serving cached models are fine. Looks like our cache-miss path is blocked.

Maya (oncall): Scope: Which customers are affected? Any dedicated/private customers?

Luca (support): So far only hosted API customers using opt-13b and similar HF-hosted artifacts. Dedicated/private unaffected (they have local cache).

Maya (oncall): Mitigation plan — immediate and short term. 1) Reduce new cold-starts by temporarily routing traffic away from instances that would trigger model fetches. 2) Increase local cache TTL? 3) Use smaller pinned fallback models for new sessions. 4) Contact HF support/ops and check status. Who can run routing change?

Jamal (eng-sre): I can push a routing policy update to favor nodes with warm caches and add a rule to reject new cold-starts for affected models (respond with 503 with helpful message) to prevent retry storms. Pushing now.

Sofia (runtime): I'll enable fallback config: for requests that would spawn a fetch for opt-13b, reply with a short explanation and route to opt-6.7b-quantized or to a cached variant. Patch: 
```json
{"fallback_model_map": {"opt-13b": "opt-6.7b-quantized"}, "cold_start_block": true}
```
Applying now.

Maya (oncall): Good. Luca: update support status page and notify top affected customers with workaround (smaller model, retries later). Use message template: 
"We're currently experiencing elevated model fetch errors from Hugging Face causing cold starts to fail. We're routing traffic to cached/smaller models as a temporary workaround. More updates soon."

Luca (support): Sending updates. Adding note to status page.

status-bot: huggingface.co reported partial outage for artifact hosting — https://status.huggingface.co/incident/xf12 (updated 09:20 UTC)

Maya (oncall): Jamal, what's the current error rate / 429 volume?

Jamal (eng-sre): 429s peaked at ~800/min across our fetch fleet around 09:13, now down to ~240/min after routing changes. Overall request success rate for model manifests is up from 12% to 58% for cached variants.

Sofia (runtime): We're also throttling our parallel fetch workers to reduce pressure on HF and avoid contributing to global rate limiting. Config snippet: 
```
MAX_PARALLEL_FETCH=4  # was 16
FETCH_RETRY_BACKOFF=[1,2,5,10]
```
This will slow recovery but reduce error amplification.

Maya (oncall): Action list (live):
- Jamal: confirm routing changes propagated and monitor 5xx/latency (in progress)
- Sofia: confirm fallback map applied and ensure logs include reason code so we can report to customers (in progress)
- Luca: customer comms + status page (in progress)
- Maya: coordinate with HF support and oncall handoff at 10:00 UTC (I'll escalate if needed)

Jamal (eng-sre): Routing change confirmed propagated to 6 regions. Metrics: cold-start-induced 503s reduced by ~70% in those regions.

Sofia (runtime): Fallback map active. Added a flag so we can revert quickly. Also pre-warming script queued to warm cached models in low-traffic windows: 
```bash
# pre-warm cached variants to reduce future cold starts
for model in opt-6.7b-quantized opt-3b; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/warm?model=$model &
done
```
Queued.

Maya (oncall): HF support: I'm creating a ticket with our logs and the rate-limiting patterns. If they can't lift limits quickly, we'll keep the fallback plan until their status clears. Attaching log excerpt.

Jamal (eng-sre): Also adding temporary client-side caching for manifests for 30m to reduce repeat fetches across hosts. Deploying config now.

Luca (support): Sent customer blast to the handful of impacted accounts. One customer replied: "thanks — please let us know when opt-13b is back, our nightly job depends on it." Responded with ETA unclear, recommend queueing for off-peak.

status-bot: huggingface.co status updated: "Artifacts service experiencing rate limiting — mitigation in progress" (09:36 UTC)

Maya (oncall): Handoff: My shift ends at 10:00 UTC. Jamal will take follow-up on-call. Jamal, you'll coordinate with HF and keep status page updated.

Jamal (eng-sre): Taking handoff. I'll run a post-incident ticket with timeline and recommended long-term mitigations (artifact mirror, proactive warmers, rate-limited backoff improvements).

Sofia (runtime): Logged follow-ups: 1) implement an internal artifact mirror for critical models, 2) smarter pre-warm heuristics, 3) improve exponential backoff with jitter, 4) per-customer priority for fetches. I'll put PRs in next sprint.

Maya (oncall): Thanks team. If HF clears within the hour we'll revert fallbacks and monitor for increased cold starts. If not, proceed with mirror plan. Ending page — leaving notes in the incident doc.

Jamal (eng-sre): Adding final metrics snapshot to incident doc: peak 429s 800/min, mitigations reduced customer-facing 503s by 70%, fallback served ~14% of requests during the incident.

Luca (support): Status page updated and customers notified. Closing support loop for tickets that accepted fallback.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and assigned to Jamal for follow-up. Runbook links: /runbooks/model-fetch-failures, /runbooks/third-party-downtime

Maya (oncall): signing off — good work.

Jamal (eng-sre): will own postmortem and follow-ups.
